OBUIAPP_PROCESS.NAME: Check Indexing Readiness
OBUIAPP_PROCESS.DESCRIPTION: Reports whether the selected sources are ready to be indexed by the next update.database
OBUIAPP_PROCESS.HELP: Reports whether the selected sources are ready to be indexed, and what is stopping the ones that are not. It changes nothing in the database. Everything a source needs -- the pgvector extension, the runtime storage, its collection and its change capture triggers -- is created by the next update.database, because creating them while the application runs makes that update refuse to start. So the order is: configure the source, press this to check it, then run update.database. Selecting every row is a sensible way to use it, and running it again is always harmless.

OBUIAPP_PROCESS.NAME: Request Reindex
OBUIAPP_PROCESS.DESCRIPTION: Asks for the records the source already held to be indexed
OBUIAPP_PROCESS.HELP: The triggers only capture what changes from the moment they are installed, so a source configured over a table that already has rows indexes nothing until those rows are walked. Select the sources and press this button to ask for that walk; the scheduled process does it, in bounded chunks, so a table of millions of rows neither holds your session nor fills the queue faster than delivery drains it. The message tells you roughly how many records you just asked for. A source has one request for its whole life, so asking again starts it over and the counters of the previous walk are lost. A walk already in progress is left alone, and a source that could not be delivered is refused rather than queued.

OBUIAPP_PROCESS.NAME: Requeue Failed Vector Events (scoped)
OBUIAPP_PROCESS.DESCRIPTION: Puts the failed indexing events of one client, one source, or both back in the queue
OBUIAPP_PROCESS.HELP: Use it once the cause of a failure is corrected, for example a wrong API key that made the provider answer 401 or 403: those failures are never retried on their own. Leave Client empty to cover every client and Source empty to cover every source; with both empty it requeues every failed event, like the scheduled Requeue Failed Vector Events. The attempt counter is reset, so the events get a full retry budget again. Up to 1000 events are requeued per run; run it again if the message says the limit was reached.
